title: Why a small type can create so much work
teaser: Make types describe the configuration you use and the capabilities a function needs.

blocks.text: A short type name can describe a lot of possibilities. Our inferred Prisma client included every possible global field-omission map, even though we never configured global omissions. Those possibilities affected the types of model results throughout the client.

When that client crossed a transaction or extension boundary, TypeScript had to establish that the types were compatible. A few shared entry points could therefore trigger comparisons across huge model payloads. The amount of source code was a poor guide to the amount of checking work.
We made the actual configuration explicit at all five constructors and aligned the extension inputs. Here is one constructor excerpt; `adapter` is the existing database adapter:

blocks.label: Describe the configuration the application actually uses

blocks.text: Here, `undefined` is a type argument describing no global omissions. It changes no data at runtime. These generic positions belong to our generated Prisma version; check yours before copying.

blocks.label: Describe only the capability the helper needs

blocks.text: Both changes follow the same principle: ask the compiler to prove only what your application requires. The measured improvement came from the combined changes, not this `Pick` alone.
